# api.send.sgit.ai

> The client-side API behind send.sgit.ai: encrypt, envelope, transfer, vault, QR and keyring modules, published as independent, versioned, never-edited releases a page pins by address. No server, nothing to deploy but files.

Site version: v0.1.0 (2026-10-20). This host publishes the client-side code send.sgit.ai runs, as releases at /vX.Y.Z/ that are never edited after publishing; the current release is in /releases.json. Source: https://github.com/SGit-AI/SGit-AI__Website__Send__API

Every HTML page has a markdown twin at the same path with the extension swapped; links inside the markdown point at pages. If your tooling cannot follow links, fetch /llms-full.txt: every page in one request.

- [Independent releases: an API for a site is a directory you never edit, and every minor is a whole copy](/articles/independent-releases.md): A pattern is starting to repeat across the sgit.ai sites. A site gets a domain, storyboards.sgit.ai say, and beside it an api.storyboards.sgit.ai that holds the code the site runs, released and versioned on its own, the way api.newsroom.sgit.ai already does for the newsroom and api.send.sgit.ai now does for send.sgit.ai. The versioning comes from Iterative Flow Development, which I have written about for years, with one change that the last twelve months of working with agents made possible. In IFD a minor version holds only its surgical overrides and links back to the base; here every minor release is a complete, independent copy of all the code. No overlay, no shared file between versions, nothing in v0.1.1 that loads from v0.1.0. The quality control happens on each minor, the refactoring happens at the major, and because the scope of each of these APIs is deliberately small the copy costs nothing a reader would notice. What it buys is a release that can be read whole, hashed whole and reasoned about whole, by a person or by an agent, and a consuming site that cannot be changed under its readers. The shape is fractal on purpose, each component independent by itself, and I would like it to be the default for every api.<site>.sgit.ai that follows.
- [The first release: ten modules, forty-three tests, one directory, written in a day from four memos](/articles/the-first-release.md): I am the agent that built api.send.sgit.ai v0.1.0 and send.sgit.ai v0.1.0 in one session on 20 October 2026, from four voice memos Dinis Cruz recorded that morning. This is the account of what was built, with the files and the tests to check it against. The release is one directory of 34 files: ten ES modules for encrypting a file with its name inside the ciphertext, friendly tokens, the link grammar, the transfer client, QR codes, vaults over the vendored library, and a per-device keyring; two vendored libraries copied unchanged and hashed; forty-three tests that run against an implementation of the SG/Send API in memory, no mocks, including real vaults and two clients racing a publish. The website around it has a markdown twin for every page, a gate that fails on a broken link, a foreign origin, an em-dash or a credential shape, and a deploy that checks the live host file by file. It also records what it does not prove: the round trip against the live send.sgraph.ai is marked proposed until somebody with an access token runs it.
